meta.title: Independent Contractor Agreement Template (Free) | Workmatic
meta.description: Download a free Independent Contractor Agreement template. Professional starting-point contract for hiring contractors. Includes payment terms, IP assignment, termination, and liability clauses.

subtitle: A professional starting-point template for hiring independent contractors. Covers scope, payment, IP ownership, confidentiality, and termination.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Scope of Services
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Vague scope leads to scope creep. Define deliverables, timelines, and acceptance criteria explicitly.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Payment Terms
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Net-30 or Net-60 favors the client. Push for Net-15 or payment upon milestone completion.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Intellectual Property Assignment
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Ensure work product IP transfers to you upon full payment. Watch for overbroad clauses claiming pre-existing IP.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Termination
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Both parties should be able to terminate with reasonable notice. Avoid lock-in without cause.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Liability Limitation
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Contractor liability should be capped (e.g., fees paid in last 12 months). Unlimited liability is a red flag.

key_clauses_to_watch.title: Confidentiality
key_clauses_to_watch.why_it_matters: Mutual confidentiality protects both sides. Define what's confidential and for how long.

faq.question: Is this template legally binding?
faq.answer: This template is a professional starting point. When properly executed by both parties, it can form a binding contract. However, laws vary by jurisdiction and specific circumstances. Consider having a qualified attorney review your final agreement.

faq.question: Can I use this for international contractors?
faq.answer: This template is designed for US domestic engagements. For international contractors, you'll need to address jurisdiction, governing law, tax treaty implications, and local labor law classification risks. Consult local counsel.

faq.question: What's the difference between an employee and independent contractor?
faq.answer: Classification depends on control, independence, and economic reality tests (varying by state and federal law). Misclassification carries significant penalties. This template assumes a valid independent contractor relationship.

faq.question: Does this template include a non-compete?
faq.answer: No. Non-competes are increasingly restricted or unenforceable in many US states. Consider a narrowly tailored non-solicitation clause instead, and check your state's current laws.
